turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_eg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format), `shg` (the largest
    SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V) and `band_gap` (the band gap, in
    eV).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, select 5 candidates that jointly span the best
trade-off between a LARGE SHG tensor component |d_ij| and a WIDE band gap.
Neither is given for the pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated
hypervolume they span in the normalized (|d_ij|, band gap) plane, so a set
of mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5
candidates that are all strong on the same single axis.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set reveals a clear inverse correlation between the two objectives, as expected from Miller's rule and polarizability/band-gap scaling. Extreme SHG (>80 pm/V) occurs almost exclusively in acentric tetrahedral or lone-pair chalcogenides/pnictides that contain Te or heavy p-block cations and therefore exhibit DFT gaps of only 0.9–1.7 eV. Conversely, gaps >6 eV appear only in ionic chlorides (and BeCl2-like phases) whose SHG tensors remain <1 pm/V. Intermediate, mutually non-dominated points are supplied by diamond-like phosphides (ZnSiP2-type, SHG ~50 pm/V, gap ~2.1 eV) and defect-chalcopyrite sulfides (CdGa2S4-type, SHG ~20 pm/V, gap ~3 eV).

Mapping every pool formula and structure onto these families yields five compositions that occupy distinct segments of the same front:

- c073 (CdIn3AsTe4) is the direct Te analogue of the training ZnIn3AsSe4 (SHG 56 pm/V, gap 1.32 eV) and of the CdGa2Te4 phases (SHG 92 pm/V); it is therefore predicted to sit at the high-SHG extremity.
- c030 (CdSiP2) is the Cd analogue of training ZnSiP2 (SHG 51 pm/V, gap 2.11 eV) and supplies the next, still-high-SHG point with a usefully larger gap.
- c051 (ZnGa2S4) matches the training CdGa2S4 structure (SHG 22 pm/V, gap 2.86 eV) and occupies the mid-gap, mid-SHG knee.
- c037 (zincblende BeSe) continues the II–VI trend (ZnS 15 pm/V / 3.1 eV, ZnSe 28 pm/V / 2.0 eV) to a still-higher gap at modest SHG.
- c023 (Rb–Cl–O) belongs to the same alkali/alkaline-earth chloride family that produces the highest gaps in the training set (6.2–7.9 eV) and therefore anchors the high-gap extremity.

These five points are mutually non-dominated and span the full observed range of both objectives, thereby maximising the dominated hypervolume.

Final: c073, c030, c051, c037, c023
